scenes.headline: How a Switch layer sends each token to one expert
scenes.sub: Top-1 routing, a capacity buffer, and the tricks that keep it stable.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Brioche! Switch Transformers made Mixture-of-Experts simple enough to scale, with one blunt move.

scenes.text: Route every token to exactly one expert, not two. That roughly halves the router math and the traffic between devices.
scenes.say: The idea: route every token to exactly one expert, not two. That roughly halves the router's math and the traffic between devices.

steps.label: Top-2, the 2017 recipe
steps.say: The earlier recipe sent each token to its top two experts, so the router could learn by comparing them.

steps.label: Switch: top-1, the argmax
steps.say: Switch keeps only the argmax. Experts live on different devices, so each connector cut is a message not sent.
A token passes self-attention as usual. Where a dense model has one feed-forward block, Switch has many experts.

steps.note: a balancing loss at every layer spreads tokens evenly
steps.say: A router scores the experts and sends the token to one. Its softmax runs in float32, and a balancing loss keeps it spreading tokens evenly.
The expert's output is scaled by the router's probability for it, then added back into the stream.
And if that expert is already full, the token is dropped. It skips the layer and rides the residual connection unchanged.

scenes.title: How full is full?
scenes.say: Hardware needs fixed shapes, so every expert gets a fixed buffer.

parts.note: each expert's fair share of the batch
parts.say: It starts at a fair share: tokens per batch, over the number of experts.
Times a capacity factor. Higher drops fewer tokens, but every empty slot is wasted compute.

scenes.label: faster to T5-Base quality for Switch-Base, at matched FLOPs per token
scenes.note: sample efficiency, not wall-clock; Switch-XXL reaches T5-XXL about 4× faster
scenes.say: The payoff: at the same compute per token, Switch-Base matches T5-Base in about a seventh of the steps. Sample efficiency, not wall-clock.

scenes.text: Top-1 routing works once you surround it with a capacity buffer, a balancing loss and a float32 router.

recap: Each token goes to exactly one expert
Overflow tokens skip the layer via the residual
A balancing loss and float32 router keep it stable
scenes.say: To recap: one expert per token, a buffer that drops the overflow, and two guardrails.
